extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants, owners, and their representatives (including non‑attorney filers and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing responses to USPTO trademark office actions (nonfinal and final), including how to use TEAS, substantive and procedural response strategies, and where to find help or resources. Focused on prosecution before the USPTO examining attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark identifies source and distinguishes goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark: Identifies the source of goods and services; Distinguishes them from the goods and services of another party; Provides legal protection for a brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: You are not 'buying' a trademark
rubrics_metrics.description: Reminder that applicants are not 'buying' a trademark; trademark rights are not purchased by filing/fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: Not every trademark is registrable; filing fees are not refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action definition and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Office action — Official letter that USPTO examining attorney issues after reviewing trademark application; Notification provided by email; Available to read and download via Trademark Status and Document Retrieval system (TSDR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TSDR link: https://tsdr.uspto.gov/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the common types of office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Common types: Nonfinal office action; Final office action; Denial of request for reconsideration; Examiner’s amendment; Priority action; Suspension letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different types have different procedural effects and response requirements (see individual entries for nonfinal/final).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfinal office action: first refusals/requirements — response required
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfinal office action raises any refusal(s) or requirement(s) for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires response for application to move forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final office action: maintains refusals/requirements — response required or abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Final office action maintains and continues any remaining refusal(s) or requirement(s) for final time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires response unless applicant decides not to continue with application.

rubrics_metrics.name: File responses using TEAS response forms
rubrics_metrics.description: File using the Trademark Electronic Application System (TEAS) response forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response link available through the office action or the USPTO website (www.uspto.gov/trademarks/apply/response-forms). Use the TEAS response form to submit your reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the office action carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: All situations — Read the office action carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful reading ensures you identify all refusals and requirements to be addressed in your response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t procrastinate
rubrics_metrics.description: All situations — Don’t procrastinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely responses are required; delays can lead to abandonment or missed opportunities to resolve issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: When discussion with examining attorney is suggested, use it
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining attorney suggests discussion — Call or email to discuss application issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The office action will specifically state when this option is available; discussions can clarify issues and possibly resolve refusals before filing a formal response.

rubrics_metrics.name: When discussion is not suggested, respond completely using TEAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion not suggested — Respond completely, addressing all issues; Use TEAS response form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examining attorney did not offer discussion, you should prepare a full written response that addresses each refusal and requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you disagree with a refusal or requirement, educate the examining attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: If you disagree with refusal or requirement — Educate the examining attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conclusory arguments; argue the evidence; submit new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conclusory arguments; support positions with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conclusory arguments when contesting a refusal or requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual, documentary, or legal evidence and reasoning rather than mere assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit new evidence when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When contesting a refusal or requirement, submit new evidence to support your position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence can change the examining attorney's view; ensure evidence directly addresses the legal/ factual basis of the refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Section 2(d) refusals (likelihood of confusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to Section 2(d) refusal — Check status of cited trademarks; Argue no likelihood of confusion exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether cited registrations are live/abandoned/limited and craft arguments (e.g., differences in marks, goods/services, trade channels, consumer sophistication) demonstrating no likelihood of confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Section 2(e)(1) refusals (descriptiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to Section 2(e)(1) refusal — Argue trademark does not describe the goods and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative actions: Amend goods and services to limit scope; Accept an alternative identification if suggested by the examining attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to 'indefinite identification' requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to 'indefinite ID' requirement — Consider suggestions in office action; Propose acceptable wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember: Cannot broaden scope of identification; Cannot 'undo' amendments to your identification after you make them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to disclaimer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding to disclaimer requirement — Consider suggestion in office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examiner's guidance on disclaimers where appropriate; disclaimers may be required for descriptive/unregistrable matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use USPTO resources for substantive and technical help
rubrics_metrics.description: For substantive questions: contact assigned examining attorney or supervisor of assigned examining attorney. For technical questions: email TEAS@uspto.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also use TSDR, USPTO website guidance pages, videos, toolkits, IP Identifier, and the Trademark Assistance Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Assistance Center contact and limitations of USPTO help
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark Assistance Center — Main support center for all trademark customers (phone and email provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO does not provide legal advice, does not enforce legal rights, and does not recommend specific private attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of scams and non‑attorney filing firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution: scam alert — Beware of scams; Beware of non-attorney filing firms; Beware of misleading notices and offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See USPTO pages on TM fraud, filing firms, and trademark solicitations for details and examples.
